FAILED ASSAULT Date: [Scribbled out]
Last night our commissar ordered an attack on the forward enemy trench. We've been trying to probe their defences for at least a week now, but as typical of the republic, this trench is stupidly fortified! So much concrete it would make an ancient soviet or a fascist blush. We couldn't find any clear weaknesses in their position. Many machine guns, some bunkers, and even what looked like auto cannons!

Enough firepower to wipe out a hundred men in an instant! But our commissars & officers felt otherwise, thinking a large sudden attack could catch them off guard & even have them running into the blizzard so we can pick them off. Well, they couldn't have been more wrong. Almost as soon as we left the safety of our trenches, the entire field was filled with bullets & the trench lit up like fireworks! Those in the front were cut down in mere seconds.

Me & my comrades quickly dove back into our trench to escape the barrage, but some of our comrades were not so lucky. Many trying to crawl back inside while bullets wailed & impaled them from behind, making sure they didn't come back. One, a young fresh conscript from Nosko station, was close to getting back in. I wanted to get back out & try to save him, but I knew that would ultimately kill me as well. The boy was struck moments later like all the rest.
Life soon drained from his eyes, turning them into glass. If only his sacrifice could have gone to something greater than a single trench.

BODY IN THE SNOW Date: [Scribbled out]
Last week I made a personal note about our failed night time attack on the enemy trench. And in that note I mentioned the boy from Nosko station who was killed during said attack. His body is right in front of my post. And his empty eyes are staring right at me! When looking over the horizon at the enemy positions, I can see them. Looking at me. Watching me every second.

There's no ignoring it either. No matter what I can see them. Sometimes... I even stare right back at them. Right back into those cold hollow eyes as if I'm trying to appease or acknowledge what they are doing! Its making me feel sick. Hopefully when the blizzard gets stronger it will blanket him in snow.

Date: [Scribbled out]
That fucking corpse! The boys body! It's still staring at me! The blizzard has covered most of him in snow but has conveniently left his fucking eyes untouched! Even in heavy fog, I still see them! And I swear, it's even getting closer! Moving forward little by little every damn night! This isn't even possible! I haven't said a word to my comrades about this. Been keeping an ear out for any mention of this.

If I wasn't the only one seeing this... it would make me feel better. But no. I haven't heard shit from anyone about fucking corpses. Nobody has even fucking acknowledged its existence! I'm truly alone in this. I'm the only one who can see... him. I know it's him. Haunting me. Torturing me. I can't even sleep. I dream about him crawling his way into our trench and killing me. Putting his frozen hand over my mouth as he stares blankly into my eyes!

And then I wake up. Restless. Cold. Gasping for air. I just want it to stop! He's angry that I didn't try to rescue him, but I had no choice god damnit!! I've been in this frozen hell for four years!! I CANT die now!! I wanna see my family again!! If I went out there I would have been on the snow just like you!! So leave me the fuck alone!!

I know what he wants. I finally get it. After a month of his torment I finally know what he wants. I need... I MUST bring him back!! I will get him! Tonight, when it gets really dark I'll crawl my way to him & drag him back here! Then I'll be forgiven! And it will all stop! No more nightmares, no more whispers, no more of anything! He'll go home and I can keep fighting this stupid war! Then I'll be home eventually! Everything will be set right!

It's time. I can toss these stupid notes into a fire when I get back. If anyone finds these I'd almost certainly get committed, which is no better than dying after four years of war.

My time in the 183rd was a short but ill-fated journey towards what was once known as Core Systems. There, a grim event took place that would later be termed only as ''The Rapture''. Dozens of critical star systems were seemingly erased from existence and the Unitan nation plunged into its two-decade long power struggle.

Our mission wasn't that of politics or military action, but one of an expedition not seen in eons. We were commissioned by a circle of extraordinarily wealthy corporate shareholders to make the plunge into the space that used to house the core planets. Our journey there was unremarkable. As expected, the charted space of the various stars and its celestial bodies simply did not exist anymore.

It was not until attempts by the fleet to make the attempted hyperspace jump home did we recognize the severe danger we were all about to be thrown into. There was no spooling of the Hyperspace Drives. Some sort of interference from an area of space we now refer to as ''The Exclusion Zone'', which completely locked up the function of the wormhole engines we relied on for inter-system travel.

We had to rely on the Alcubierre drives to make the slow journey home. Rationing could keep the whole fleet up for a few months at most, but it was evident that the Alcubierres would take years at best to reach the nearest starport. The servicemen and women of the 183rd needed someone to guide their hand through the void. We had to scoop hydrogen emissions from stars and stop the situation from becoming hopeless.

It's of a terrible irony that much of our own crew did not die from starvation, but from internal conflict on the guidance of the mission. They had to be put down, lest the entire fleet be doomed to nihilistic surrender.

Im sorry to not have been waiting for you in bed this morning. 
For not being anywhere inside our little cabin when you got up today. Or as you will now realize, nowhere near our home & community.

This must be very confusing & strange to you and I am very sorry.
Ever since we first meet each other in middle school, I had a spark for you. 
Tried to deny it to all my friends, but I knew deep inside I was just speaking a bunch of bull and just trying to not get picked on.

Then years later we had our first date in that dirty retro drive in theater that we both loved.

You touched my hand that night when we watched one of those ancient horror movies with the old school flesh eaters.

Next day you & I had our first kiss before class. And then few years after that we got engaged & married.
Our marriage was the happiest day of my life. Nothing could or would ever beat it.

Life was good for a while. Me working as a forest ranger & you getting involved in local community projects.
We had our differences no doubt. One of those being that you were much more in touch with the spiritual & faith side of things.

I never really cared much. Church just wasn't really in my life like that. My favorite hobby was of course camping out which you didn't care so much for.

Unfortunately, we had our share of hardships too. The worst being our little flower Daisy. We were left in a dark hole what seemed endless. Nothing was ever the same again. And it felt like nothing would ever BE the same again.

But when this group of religious folk came into town looking for extra hands to help with a building project, things seemed to finally turn around for the best.
Felt like the best of all worlds, for the both of us.

I got to spend more time outdoors and teach some folk some basic survival skills. You got to get closer to god & help build a new community at the same time.
And when you came to me asking if we could go & live with them at their new little commune I honestly couldn't help but say yes. Anything for us to both be happy.
At the time it seemed like the best decision we could have made. We were happy & excited for the future again. Life didn't feel so static & grey day in & day out.

When the shuttle took us to an empty plot of land on this backwater planet, I will admit to being slightly skeptical given your history with being in the wilderness.

But you didn't complain none. Not one bit. Hell, I think I was the only one really complaining at the time while everyone else was gitty as one could ever be.

This optimism didn't last much long for me though. All started going down hill since my first church session. The things that were spoken of were not from any holy bible I ever heard of.

Sure, I was again not the spiritual one. But even still it felt wrong. Something felt very wrong. In the end though, I just tried to ignore it so that we could just keep living our new perfect life.

Especially didn't wanna dissapoint or upset you. But as the weeks became months, and the months turned to years, I started to feel like this was less of a paradise & more of a prison.

Then, on that faithful day, a great fireball came from the sky, and out crawled many many people. Stranded and left with nothing.

I was hoping, like good Christians, we would go help these people.

Shelter them, feed them, clothe them. The virtues that all Christians are supposed to be taught. Ones you even held very strongly, more than anyone else I had ever known.

When our pastor gathered us into the church soon after, and started spewing out all that hateful garbage. It was the final bit of confirmation for everything I had been feeling for years.

They had come to our gates many times. And every time they arive we give them screams, shouts, & bullets. I stopped taking guard duty from that point on, and switched to foraging.

''Foraging'', or just camping out in the woods alone for a few days, was the only bit of peace I could bring to myself for at least the next several years.

I was idiotically content to keep this cycle going. I didn't want to confront the reality of our situation, and how much it had devolved. Life was back to being a grey blur of nothingness.

Each day just as meaningless as the last. Then I had another realization. This was not a prison, this was purgatory. I felt like I could do nothing. Nothing but watch myself go to waste & my wife lose her mind.

Seeing you repeat the retoric from the pastor. It made me mad, and sad, and then I just stopped caring. This place was made to suck the soul out of us.

But I was still somehow not pushed yet. It wasn't until a few nights ago, that I got pushed too far. It's been years & the group hasn't been growing. 

If anything we are going to be dying in mass soon with all this filth everywhere that we for some insane reason refuse to get rid of in some petty effort to starve the people outside of literally anything.

Pastor has said it's time for us to start planting the seeds to our trees. You told me the same thing. The excitement in your eyes. It was unbearable. You wanted to bring children here.

All because he said so & to do it. Daisy, and the pain that followed, all seemingly forgotten. Blown away into the wind.

Well, I will not forget. I will not allow myself to forget our little baby girl. The one we never even got to hold before she was carried by god. I won't allow it.

So I left. Not to forage. But for good. With some basic supplies & a couple guns. I wish I could bring you, my beloved, my shining light, with me out of this place. This hell. But I know better.

My Lyn, is gone. The woman I married decades ago now, is not here anymore. She died along with her daughter in that hospital bed. It just took me countless years to finally realize it.

And now, I must move on, and not again let the weeks turn to months, and the months turn to years in another blur. Otherwise, I too will die like the rest of my family.

When stopping by another station today we saw a crowd gathered near the towns coal mine. They were screaming & shouting about the same old shit. How their work hours were unfair & that they deserved at least a whole weekend off or so from work among other things. We approached them like we always do with any angry crowd & told them the same old shit. ''We need you to keep working so that everyone around the Republic has enough coal.''

''No work means less coal to be shipped around for everyone.'' ''Less coal means no heating.'' ''And less coal also means the trains will slow down or stop.'' After giving the usual speech that we must have given a thousand times already, the crowd unsurprisingly got upset about their ridiculous demands not being met and started swearing at us. Nothing we hadn't heard before. But then, someone said something we hadn't heard before. ''Fuck the Republic pigs!! We will join the People's Party!!''.

After that, the bastards started chanting bullshit People's Party rhetoric and their motto, showing their true colors. Yeah, that really got us pissed. Our ''people'' siding with the enemy we have to fight every single day so that they can live fairly comfortable lives. We all gave this glancing look to each other. All of us on the same page, including our NCO. Without saying a word, we swiftly pulled our rifles up towards the crowd, and held the trigger.

After it was all said & done we just stood there. Felt like we stood on that ground for a million years with nothing but the wind howling and snow blowing into our faces. Then our NCO told us to pack up & get back into the train. And so we did. Not saying a single word till after we were on our way. It's not that any of us felt guilty. Far from. We just couldn't believe nearly an entire town had stooped low enough to give themselves to the Reds.

The incident was reported to high command soon after by our NCO. We were expecting some sort of punishment for this, but it never came. Right after our NCO was finished radioing command he went to the large map we had in the train and crossed out the town's name with a marker. And that told us everything we needed to know.

To my dear sister Tenuzen, I send this letter bearing my notes on what was once known as the 'Human Village'. I have found their new religion utterly baffling and contradictory to all rationale and logic. They have established a new institute they name the 'Syncretic Church' which they claim is in reverance to a deity they simply call ''God''. It is confusing, as there are already many Gods in Gensokyo, yet they revere one simply named as such.

For hundreds of years they have worshipped the deities of Japan and Gensokyo for as long as they have existed. Yet as I understand, the Barrier collapsed two-hundred years ago which left us open to barbarian influences. People have appeared in this world not of our own, and they bring with them books of foreign deities. They have so willingly accepted these strange beliefs.

This religion of theirs is based on apparent nothings. They revere a God that does not appear to them, that does not speak to them, nor does it seem to even bestow the simplest form of direct justice. They have discovered commandments of their God, with the most baseline of simple morals. They claim that simple goodwill and faith is more than enough to bestow good fortune. That doesn't seem very fair for a deity to receive so little for so much reward. Any other would ask for sacrifice.

When one murders another, there is no justice and no spirit to deliver it. When a storm destroys a man's farm, no prayer or sacrifice will help that soul. When one asks for even a simple answer, their God leaves them with silence. Have they deluded themselves? It seems more like their faith is hope where there is none, so that they can worship a God that either doesn't exist or simply doesn't care. It's just not rational in the face of all the other deities.

I also received your letter from last week in regards to the completion of the embassy the humans have built. As far as I understand, it is for them to develop better 'diplomatic' relations with us? Momiji endorses it, but it is a concept I am not familiar with. Not like we needed them to build our city either. I hope to see you in town next week, so long as the humans aren't too slow getting my armor done. Honestly, 50 years isn't enough time to learn anything.

Research at the YW-CORP have revealed a potential new groundbreaking substance that could revolutionize the way we reconnect neural pathways.

A few hundred years ago you could hook your brain to a computer and be imprinted with the memories needed to operate a cybernetic arm or even machinery with a mere surgical process and a small cybernetic implant. Though the technology was experimental at the time, the outlawing of ''unethical'' practices such as AI and cybernetic developments at the time caused the technology to be ruthlessly pursued into extinction.
Such a violent history was not completely unwarranted, as multiple colonies rose in rebellion, led by AI governors.

YW CORP Lead Scientist Shukijo Barret posits that the new substance known as YW-11 can be imprinted onto an existing mind by injecting the substance into a host. Clinical trials with mice have been relatively successful so far. The substance, over a period of a few days, takes on a mind-bogglingly complex pattern within the host. After a suitable amount of time, the substance is extracted carefully and then injected onto a new host.

Over dozens of mice testing, the new host begins to take on the traits of the original imprinted mice. Shujiko claims that this is how the memories are copied over, as the new host is imprinted with the new skills of the previous host. Imagine if you will, that you wanted to say... play a guitar, write a book, or draw like an artist. You'd need years to practice just one of these skills, right? And that's assuming you have the time outside of work to even get a start on any of them.

With YW-11, you could learn a new skill in the fraction of that time. You could play like a famous musician or draw like a renowned artist with imprints of their memories. You could operate heavy machinery or fly spacecraft, with only a fraction of the time needed. Shujiko admits that YW-11 requires more experimentation. Scientists are holding their heads high however, as this could be something that changes the way humanity thinks, forever.

Generation Ships and FTL

In 2200, The United States of America commissioned the first generation of Subspace Generation Ships made expressly for the purpose of colonized designated planets with the high potential for habitation. These vessels were powered by subspace engines alone, lacking the advantages of modern warp drives today.
Although primitive by today's standards, these Generation Ships paved the way for more advanced void-faring vessels and the common Alcubierre and Hyperspace Drives.

The Alcubierre Drive ''pushes'' a vessel through real-space, appearing to the pilot as if they were literally accelerating to speeds beyond light which consequently makes visual navigation impossible once beyond the speed of light. In the United State's attempt to weaponize the original versions of the Alcubierre Drive it was found that not only were gravity wells around celestial bodies able to force a vessel out of this warp method, a sufficiently large space station could achieve a similar effect.
This is of course ignoring the fact that Alcubierre warps are not accurate and could very easily miss by margins of hundreds of thousands of kilometres, even with a ''static'' target in stable orbit.

The Hyperspace Drive is the primary engine used by modern void-faring vessels when navigating between star systems, functioning as a wormhole engine. Early versions would require weeks to spool fully. Once spooled, what is theorized as a realspace rip is created and the vessel enters a secondary dimension where movement within is amplified by extreme magnitudes in realspace.

A vessel that may have been observed to travel perhaps only a few kilometres in this alternative dimension may exit at a designated target dozens of lightyears away. Visual observers of this extradimensional realm describe it as ''blindingly unremarkable. A completely white void with no features.'' The Hyperspace drive suffers from similar gravity well limitations at the star level, with miscalculated travel into a system's well resulting in the violent but survivable return to realspace.

Projection-87 is to remain locked in a vehicle holding cell converted to function as a containment chamber. No individuals are to enter P-87 unless for the purposes of testing. Hatches to enter P-87 are to remain key-locked.

Projection-87 is an incredibly large Main Battle Tank presumably Unitan in origin, given the markings present, though no known models of such a tank appear to exist. P-87 exhibits no anomalous properties aside from a staggering resilience to modern ballistic weaponry. P-87s properties are exhibited when an individual capable of operating vehicles of similar configuration seats themselves in P-87, from which intense mental fatigue overtakes the individual.

P-87 materialized during a surge test performed on D-22, appearing some distance above the ground. The falling mass of metal crushed D-22 and 2 other staff. Security teams were deployed under the assumption that a hostile force was attacking the facility, with Complex-[REDACTED] entering lockdown for approximately 48 hours.

Testing Log B [[]/[]/[]

Human Male, 41, same subject as before. Subject seated himself inside of P-87. After 30 minutes, subject began to sleep. Subject was left inside P-87 for approximately 3 days. Subject expired from dehydration, and the test concluded. Body incinerated.

Permission was granted to test a variety of weapons against the armor of P-87. The lore of the Ancient One, rewarded to those who defeat it.

Years before Earth's destruction, a lone figure entered the Bossvault. It was a small winged creature, none other than the penguin pirate Dreadwing. Without being detected by the ancient security systems, Dreadwing salvaged a large amount of ancient materials. After leaving, Dreadwing used the ancient materials to build a spacecraft more powerful than any in the known universe.

Once he turned it on, however, the machine began scanning the area and acting puzzled as if it had a mind of its own. It seemed the ancient materials and the mysterious core Dreadwing used for the spacecraft's power source had created a "living" machine with its own independent behavior. The spacecraft began firing powerful energy bolts at Dreadwing, but he swiftly dashed through an escape hatch where the machine could not reach him. Having lost sight of its target it left Dreadwing's base and instinctively flew toward the planet

where the Bossvault was. As it passed through the galaxy and over planets, people who believed in legends of ancient beings referred to the strange spacecraft traveling over the planet as The Ancient One. Dreadwing, who had learned his lesson about tampering with such power, decided to build his spacecraft out of more conventional materials. As for The Ancient One, it eventually found its way back to the Bossvault and currently guards it against anyone who dares try to steal the ancients' secrets.
